headline: Approved $173,714 energy grant, named 617 Lexington Street school building, and referred zoning cases for 181-185 Felton Street and 20 Williams Street to committee.
summary: The Council held five public hearings on zoning, street openings, a special permit, and a fuel storage license, and referred each to committee. It also approved several committee recommendations, including a Green Communities Grant of $173,714, acceptance of fitness equipment for the Fire Department, three licenses, and naming the 617 Lexington Street building after John J "Jack" Daddona. The Council approved the November 2026 Election Warrant and referred several Community Preservation Committee funding requests to the Long Term Debt and Capital Planning Committee.
decisions: Approved the regular City Council meeting minutes of September 14, 2026.
Referred the Zoning Ordinance Amendment at 181-185 Felton Street to the Ordinances and Rules Committee.
Referred the Street Opening at 205 Second Avenue to the Public Works and Public Safety Committee.
Referred the Street Opening at 1-141 South Street to the Public Works and Public Safety Committee.
Referred the Special Permit application at 20 Williams Street to the Ordinances and Rules Committee and recessed the hearing to November 23, 2026.
Referred the Fuel Storage License for 40-50 & 60 Sylvan Road to the Licenses and Franchises Committee.
Referred the Mayor's request regarding the Lawrence School Building to the Committee of the Whole.
Referred the Mayor's request regarding the Government Center building and land to the Committee of the Whole.
Approved a request to invite a Suicide Prevention Program clinician to a future Committee of the Whole meeting; the resolution was referred to the Committee of the Whole.
Approved the Resolution in Honor of Recovery Awareness Month 2026.
Referred the Special Act on Health Insurance Coverage for the Mayor's office to the Ordinances and Rules Committee.
Approved acceptance of fitness equipment from Core Development & Management and Planet Fitness for the Fire Department.
Approved acceptance of the Green Communities Competitive Grant in the amount of $173,714.
Approved the Secondhand Dealers' license for Pedals & Powder, LLC at 85 River Street.
Approved the Class II license renewal for New England Transit Sales, Inc. at 215 Lexington Street.
Approved naming the 617 Lexington Street building "The John J 'Jack' Daddona Education Center."
Referred the CPC recommendation for $320,000 of CPA funds for Window Restoration at Gore Place to the Long Term Debt and Capital Planning Committee.
Referred the CPC recommendation for $85,000 of CPA funds for Exterior Restoration of Community Day Center at 20 Felton Street to the Long Term Debt and Capital Planning Committee.
Referred the CPC recommendation for $50,768 of additional CPA funds for Steeple Preservation and Restoration at First Parish Church to the Long Term Debt and Capital Planning Committee.
Approved the November 2026 Election Warrant.

plain_text:
1
Waltham City Council 
Minutes of the Meeting of 
September 28, 2026
President Logan called the meeting to order at 7:30 p.m. 
 
Artie Kronenfeld from the Waltham Times was recognized as recording the meeting.
Present: Bradley-MacArthur, Brasco, Dunn, Durkee, Harris, Hanley, Katz, King, LaCava, LaFauci, 
LeBlanc, McLaughlin, Tzioumis, Vidal and President Logan. 
Absent: None.
Board of Survey & Planning
Present: M. Justin Barrett (remote), William Creonte, Wayne Keefner, S. Anthony DeVito, Brian
Moroney and Mila Tarallo.
Absent: None.
City Clerk Vizard recited the Council Prayer followed by President Logan leading all present in the 
Pledge of Allegiance. Councillor Durkee spoke on September, being Suicide Prevention Month and
asked for a moment of silence for all the military that have served past and present.
Councillor LeBlanc moved approval of the regular City Council meeting minutes of September 14, 
2026. The motion was approved by a voice vote. 
Clerk Vizard read Rule 86.
First Joint Public Hearing: Zoning Ordinance Amendment at 181 – 185 Felton Street
Clerk Vizard read the public hearing notice. Attorney Michael Connors of 689 Main Street, 
Waltham, MA representing the petitioner, spoke on the matter. Tom Benevides of 308 River 
Street, #3, Waltham, MA and Deb Herman of 3 Grant Place, #2, Waltham, MA spoke in favor of
the matter. 7 people stood in favor of the matter. With no one else in favor, no one in opposition 
and no one in a neutral position to the ordinance President Logan closed that part of the public 
hearing and opened the hearing up to questions from Councillors. No Councillors had comments.
Board of Survey and Planning members, Mr. Creonte and Mr. Moroney asked questions. 
Attorney Connors provided answers. With no further questions President Logan closed the 
Public Hearing and referred the matter to the Ordinances and Rules Committee. Mr. Creonte
stated the Board of Survey and Planning would be meeting on October 7, 2026 at 6:00 p.m. at 
Government Center.
President Logan called a recess at 8:10 p.m. while the Board of Survey and Planning cleared the 
room. 
President Logan called the meeting back to order at 8:13 p.m.
Second Public Hearing: 17-25 Street Opening at 205 Second Avenue
Clerk Vizard read the public hearing notice. Mary Mulroney, 201 Rivermore Street, West Roxbury, 
MA representing the petitioner, spoke on the matter. With no one else in favor, no one in opposition 
and no one in a neutral position to the license, President Logan closed that part of the public hearing 
and opened the hearing up to questions from Councillors. Councillor LaFauci asked questions. Ms. 
Mulroney provided answers. With no further questions President Logan closed the public hearing 
and referred the matter to the Public Works and Public Safety Committee.
2
Third Public Hearing: 17-25 Street Opening at 1-141 South Street
Clerk Vizard read the public hearing notice. Mary Mulroney, 201 Rivermore Street, West Roxbury, 
MA representing the petitioner, spoke on the matter. With no one else in favor, no one in opposition 
and no one in a neutral position to the license, President Logan closed that part of the public hearing 
and opened the hearing up to questions from Councillors. Councillor Katz asked questions. Ms. 
Mulroney provided answers. With no further questions President Logan closed the public hearing 
and referred the matter to the Public Works and Public Safety Committee.
Fourth Public Hearing: Special Permit application at 20 Williams Street
Clerk Vizard read the public hearing notice. Attorney Joseph Connors of 404 Main Street, Waltham, 
MA representing the petitioner, spoke on the matter. Brad Upton of 25 Virginia Road, Waltham, MA
and Tom Benevides of 308 River Street, #3, Waltham, MA spoke in favor of the matter. Clerk 
Vizard read an email from Diane McElligott of 24-28 Williams Street RE tr. in favor of the matter. 
23 people stood in favor of the matter. With no one else in favor, no one in opposition and no one in 
a neutral position to the modification, President Logan closed that part of the public hearing and 
opened the hearing up to questions from Councillors. Councillors LaCava, Katz, Harris, Hanley and 
Bradley-MacArthur spoke on the matter. With no further questions President Logan referred the 
matter to the Ordinances and Rules Committee. President Logan recessed the public hearing to date 
certain of Monday, November 23, 2026 at 7:30 p.m.
Fifth Public Hearing: Fuel Storage License 40-50 & 60 Sylvan Road
Clerk Vizard read the public hearing notice. Jaime Giordana of 400 Technology Square, Cambridge, 
MA, representing the petitioner, spoke on the matter. With no one else in favor, no one in opposition
and no one in a neutral position to the modification, President Logan closed that part of the public 
hearing and opened the hearing up to questions from Councillors. Councillor LaFauci spoke on the 
matter. With no further questions President Logan referred the matter to the Licenses and Franchises 
Committee.
Communications from the Mayor
1. The Mayor respectfully requested the City Council’s recommendations with regard to the 
Lawrence School Building. Referred to the Committee of the Whole.
2. The Mayor respectfully requested the City Council’s recommendations with regard to the 
Government Center building and land. Referred to the Committee of the Whole
Resolutions, Orders and Ordinances
 Suicide Prevention Awareness Month Resolution
Clerk Vizard read the Resolution. Councillor Durkee spoke on the Resolution. Clerk Vizard 
read a request from Councillor Durkee to have a Licensed Independent Clinical Social 
Worker or a PhD from the Suicide Prevention Program, Bredford VA Healthcare System, 
200 Springs Road Bedford, MA be invited to a future Committee of the Whole meeting at 
their earliest convenience. The request was approved by a voice vote. Referred to the 
Committee of the Whole.
 Resolution in Honor of Recovery Awareness Month 2026
Clerk Vizard read the Resolution. Councillor Harris spoke on the Resolution and moved to 
suspend Rule 39 to act on the matter without Committee reference. The motion was 
approved by a voice vote. Councillor Harris moved for approval. The motion was approved
3
by a voice vote and the Resolution in Honor of Recovery Awareness Month 2026 was 
approved.
President Logan relinquished the Chair to Vice President LeBlanc.
 Special Act to Authorize City to make Health Insurance Coverage available to the office of 
the Mayor per M.G.L. c. 32B Resolution
Clerk Vizard read the Resolution. President Logan spoke on the matter. Councillors Harris 
and Bradley-MacArthur spoke on the Resolution. Referred to the Ordinances and Rules 
Committee.
Vice President LeBlanc relinquished the Chair back to President Logan.
Committee Reports
Finance
1. The Finance Committee recommended the acceptance of fitness equipment from Core 
Development & Management and Planet Fitness for the City of Waltham Fire Department 
be approved. Councillor Durkee moved that the action of the Committee be the action of the
Council. The motion was approved by a voice vote, and the matter was approved.
2. The Finance Committee recommended the acceptance of the Green Communities 
Competitive Grant in the amount of $173,714 from the Department of Energy Resources 
(DOER) Green Communities Division be approved. Councillor Durkee moved that the 
action of the Committee be the action of the Council. The motion was approved by a voice 
vote, and the matter was approved.
Licenses and Franchises
1. The Licenses and Franchises Committee recommended the Secondhand Dealers’ license 
for Pedals & Powder, LLC at 85 River Street be approved. Councillor Vidal moved that 
the action of the Committee be the action of the Council. The motion was approved by a 
voice vote, and the matter was approved.
2. The Licenses and Franchises Committee recommended the Class II license renewal for 
New England Transit Sales, Inc. at 215 Lexington Street be approved. Councillor Vidal 
moved that the action of the Committee be the action of the Council. The motion was 
approved by a voice vote, and the matter was approved.
3. The Licenses and Franchises Committee recommended the request from the Waltham 
School Committee regarding naming the 617 Lexington Street building “The John J 
“Jack” Daddona Education Center” be approved. Councillor Vidal moved that the action 
of the Committee be the action of the Council. The motion was approved by a voice vote, 
and the matter was approved.
Unfinished Business & Other Business
 CPC Recommendation for an allocation of $320,000 of CPA funds for Window 
Restoration at Gore Place.
Referred to the Long Term Debt and Capital Planning Committee.
 CPC Recommendation for an allocation of $85,000 of CPA funds for Exterior Restoration 
of Community Day Center 20 Felton Street Location.
4
Referred to the Long Term Debt and Capital Planning Committee.
 CPC Recommendation for an allocation of $50,768 of additional CPA funds for Steeple 
Preservation and Restoration at First Parish Church.
Referred to the Long Term Debt and Capital Planning Committee.
 November 2026 Election Warrant
Councillor LeBlanc moved to suspend Rule 39 to act on the matter without Committee 
reference. The motion was approved by a voice vote. Councillor LeBlanc moved approval.
The motion was approved by a voice vote and the November 2026 Election Warrant was 
approved.
Tabled Items
 66 Brewster Road (Tabled 6/9/25)
Rule 58
 Letter from Town of Lincoln regarding Bay Colony (MIRROD) Redevelopment and 
Associated Traffic Impacts on Waltham-Lincoln Border
 Mayor’s Communication regarding 240 Beaver Street
 Mayor’s Communication regarding Former Elks Building Lexington and School Street
Recessed Public Hearings
 Special Permit MICOL at 220 Moody Street recessed on 8/3/26 (10/26/26)
 Special Permit CAVA Group Inc. at 96 Tower Road recessed 8/3/26 (10/13/26)
 Special Permit Modification Dyer’s Crescent Suites, LLC 287 Crescent Street recessed 
9/14/26 (11/23/26)
 Special Permit Service Credit Union 995 Main Street recessed 9/14/26 (11/23/26)
With no further matters Councillor Brasco made a motion to adjourn. The motion was approved 
by a voice vote. President Logan declared the meeting adjourned at 9:20 p.m.
Respectfully submitted by:
Cathy Magliarditi
Executive Assistant to the City Clerk
October 5, 2026
